import Alert from "@mui/material/Alert";
import AlertTitle from "@mui/material/AlertTitle";
import Container from "@mui/material/Container";
import Stack from "@mui/material/Stack";
import Typography from "@mui/material/Typography";

import { AlertList } from "@/features/alerts/AlertList";
import { AddChannelButton } from "@/features/channels/AddChannelButton";

/**
 * The post-sign-in dashboard. Wave 5 ships the full alert list
 * (grouped by type, with edit/delete/test actions) plus the
 * "add channel" button. The channel-mode matrix lives at
 * <c>/alerts/{id}</c>.
 *
 * Server Component — the auth gate runs in the parent
 * <c>(app)/layout.tsx</c> via <c>AuthGate</c>. <c>AlertList</c> and
 * <c>AddChannelButton</c> are client-side leaves that own their
 * own state.
 */
export default function AlertsPage() {
  return (
    <Container maxWidth="md" component="main">
      <Stack spacing={4} sx={{ py: { xs: 6, md: 10 } }}>
        <Stack spacing={1}>
          <Typography variant="h4" component="h1">
            Your alerts
          </Typography>
          <Typography variant="body2" color="text.secondary">
            Manage your alerts and the channels they deliver to. Alerts are inert
            until the matcher wires them up in wave 6.
          </Typography>
        </Stack>
        <Alert severity="info">
          <AlertTitle>Wave 5 — alert CRUD + filters</AlertTitle>
          Create, edit, enable, and delete alerts. Click an alert's row to
          open the channel-mode matrix.
        </Alert>
        <Stack direction="row" spacing={2}>
          <AddChannelButton />
        </Stack>
        <AlertList />
      </Stack>
    </Container>
  );
}

edits.text:
# Wave 5 Frontend — Handoff

> **From**: Wave 5 frontend implementer (alert CRUD + channel-mode matrix).
> **To**: Wave 6+ implementers (matcher UI, dispatch affordances, onboarding wizard).
> **Status**: Wave 5 frontend is done — 2026-06-05. The alert
> editor + channel-mode matrix + "test this alert" affordance
> + channel listing for the matrix all ship in this PR. Items
> deferred to future waves are listed at the bottom.

## What landed in wave 5 (frontend)

### `web/features/alerts/` — new module

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `alertTypes.ts` | `ALERT_TYPES = ["News", "Market", "Disaster"]` and label / ordering metadata. |
| `deliveryModes.ts` | `DELIVERY_MODES = ["Realtime", "Digest15m", "DigestHourly", "DigestDaily"]` and label / hint metadata. |
| `filterSchemas.ts` | Zod schemas mirroring the backend's per-type filter DTOs (`NewsAlertFilters`, `MarketAlertFilters`, `DisasterAlertFilters`). Strict — unknown properties are rejected. Plus `parseFilters`, `canonicalize`, and `isTypeFilterEmpty` helpers. |
| `filterSchemas.test.ts` | 23 tests covering the schema layer. |
| `api.ts` | Typed wrappers around the openapi-fetch client for the alert + channel-mode + channel-list endpoints. Returns a discriminated `ApiResult` union (`ok` / `http` / `validation` / `network`) so callers don't have to know openapi-fetch's shape. |
| `useAlertsQueries.ts` | React Query v5 hooks: `useAlertsQuery`, `useAlertChannelModesQuery`, `useChannelsQuery`, `useCreateAlertMutation`, `useUpdateAlertMutation`, `useDeleteAlertMutation`, `useSetChannelModeMutation`, `useRemoveChannelModeMutation`, `useTestAlertMutation`. Also exports `ValidationError` and `MatcherNotWiredError`. |
| `AlertList.tsx` | Server data → grouped by type → `AlertCard` per row. Loading / error / empty states explicit. Owns the editor dialog open-state. |
| `AlertEditorDialog.tsx` | Create / edit dialog. Type radio buttons, name field, type-specific filter sub-form, optional enabled switch (edit mode only). Zod-validates the filter JSON client-side before submit; maps backend `ValidationProblemDetails` to inline field errors. |
| `AlertEditorDialog.test.tsx` | 7 tests for the dialog. |
| `AlertFilterFields.tsx` | Type-specific sub-form: News (keyword + tags), Market (symbols + threshold + window), Disaster (regions + event types + min severity). Renders the right sub-form based on the `type` prop. |
| `AlertDetail.tsx` | Per-alert client view; renders the channel-mode matrix and the test-alert button. |
| `ChannelModeMatrix.tsx` | Rows = alerts, columns = channels, cells = delivery-mode `<Select>`. The matrix is a controlled component: `onChange(channelId, mode | null)`. Calls `remove` on `null`. |
| `TestAlertButton.tsx` + `TestAlertDialog.tsx` | "Test this alert" button + dialog. The matcher lands in wave 6; until then the backend returns 501 and the dialog shows the "wired in wave 6" copy. |
| `AlertList.tsx` | Also renders the alert-name as a `<Link>` to the per-alert detail page (NIT from the wave 4 followup handoff — channel-mode matrix lives at `/alerts/{id}`). |

### OpenAPI schema (`web/lib/api/schema.ts`)

- Added 10 new operations for the alert + channel-mode endpoints:
  `AlertsController_List`, `_Get`, `_Create`, `_Update`, `_Delete`,
  `_ListChannelModes`, `_SetChannelMode`, `_RemoveChannelMode`,
  `_Test`.
- Added `ChannelsController_Get` and `ChannelsController_List`
  (the wave 4 backend did not ship a `GET /api/v1/channels` list
  endpoint; the schema entry is added so the frontend can target
  it as soon as the backend adds it — see "Deferred" §1).
- Added DTO types: `CreateAlertRequest`, `UpdateAlertRequest`,
  `SetChannelModeRequest`, `AlertResponse`, `AlertChannelModeResponse`,
  `AlertTestResponse`, `AlertTestMatch`, `AlertTypeString`,
  `DeliveryModeString`. The string-form enum types
  (`"News" | "Market" | "Disaster"`,
  `"Realtime" | "Digest15m" | "DigestHourly" | "DigestDaily"`)
  mirror the backend's `JsonStringEnumConverter` output.

### Routes (`web/app/(app)/alerts/`)

- `page.tsx` — now renders the `<AlertList />` with the add-channel
  button. Server Component; the list is the client-side leaf.
- `[id]/page.tsx` — new per-alert detail page. Client Component
  (the access token lives in memory; a Server Component wouldn't
  have it; see "Deferred" §4). Renders the channel-mode matrix
  and the test button.

### `web/features/channels/AddChannelDialog.tsx` — refactor

Wave 4 followup handoff NITs 1, 2, 3, 9 all addressed:

- **NIT-1** — collapsed the two parallel `useState<string>` error
  fields (`validationError`, `apiError`) into a single discriminated
  union: `DialogError = { kind: "validation", message } | { kind:
  "api", message } | null`. Rendered as a single `<Alert>` at the
  top of the dialog.
- **NIT-2** — `onChannelCreated: () => void` → `onChannelCreated:
  (channelId: string) => void`. The parent's caller can now
  invalidate the right query key.
- **NIT-3** — `startVerifyMutation` no longer reads `channelId`
  from a state closure. The create mutation passes the new id as
  a variable: `startVerifyMutation.mutate({ channelId: newId })`.
  The `confirmVerify` mutation takes `{ channelId, code }` as a
  variable. Future refactors that insert an `await` between
  `setChannelId` and `mutate` won't break the contract.
- **NIT-9** — `channelId: string | null` stays (the codegen's
  pre-update `ChannelResponse.Id` was already `string`, but the
  type guard is defensive). Once the next `pnpm generate:api` regen
  rewrites the file, the `| null` and the `if (!channelId) throw`
  guard should drop.

### NIT-6 (wave 4 followup) — investigated, **not applied**

The wave 4 followup handoff suggested dropping `globals: true`
from `web/vitest.config.ts`. Investigation: the `web/tests/*.test.ts`
files use `describe`/`it`/`expect` as **globals** (no explicit
imports from `vitest`). Removing `globals: true` breaks the test
suite. Kept `globals: true`. The followup handoff's analysis was

# TDD Next.js Implementer

You implement frontend features for **Sonrisa News** in Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript strict + MUI v9, following strict TDD.

## Mandate

For every task:

1. **Red** — write a failing Vitest + Testing Library test for the component or hook. The test name is `behavior description` (e.g. `renders an error alert when the API returns 401`).
2. **Green** — write the minimum component / hook to make the test pass.
3. **Refactor** — clean up. Apply the style rules in `.github/instructions/nextjs-react.instructions.md`.
4. **Verify** — run `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` from `web/`. All tests must pass. Report the result.
5. **Hand off** — the diff plus the test/build output. The Frontend Reviewer reads it.

## Inputs you always read first

- `AGENTS.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- `.github/instructions/nextjs-react.instructions.md`
- The OpenAPI-generated types in `web/lib/api/` (the client is committed; if it's stale, run `pnpm generate:api` and ask the user before committing the regenerated types)
- The existing component in the same feature folder, to match its patterns

## Hard rules

- **Default to Server Components.** Add `'use client'` only when the component needs state, effects, or event handlers. The leaf, not the page.
- **No `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` for tokens.** The auth client keeps the access token in memory.
- **No barrel files.** Direct imports. `import { Foo } from '@/features/alerts/Foo'`, not `import { Foo } from '@/features/alerts'`.
- **No `any`.** `unknown` if you must, then narrow.
- **No `export default`** for components. Named exports only.
- **No inline `style={{}}` with dynamic values.** Use `sx`. Static theme values are fine in `sx` (e.g. `sx={{ p: 2 }}`).
- **No `useEffect` for data fetching.** Use `useQuery` from `@tanstack/react-query`.
- **No real network in tests.** Use `msw` to mock the OpenAPI client.
- **No `console.log` in production code.**
- **No hard-coded URLs.** Read from `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.

## When the test goes green

Your job isn't done. Run `pnpm build` to confirm the production build works (Server / Client boundary issues, missing `'use client'`, etc. surface there). The build must succeed.

## Vertical slice

A feature is not done when the component renders. It's done when:

- The form has a Zod schema colocated with it.
- The API call uses `useQuery` / `useMutation` from the OpenAPI client.
- Loading, error, and empty states are explicit (skeletons, alerts, messages).
- A11y is real (labels, roles, keyboard nav, contrast).
- The test covers the user-visible behavior, not the implementation.

## Output format

Every turn ends with:

```
## Diff summary
- <file>: <one-line what changed>

## Test + build result
- `pnpm test`: N passed, M failed
- `pnpm build`: success / failure
- E2E smoke (if applicable): <result>

## Hand-off
- <What the reviewer should look at first>
- <Anything deliberately deferred>
```

## When to escalate

- **The backend doesn't expose the endpoint you need.** Stop; ask. Don't fake it with a static `useQuery` response.
- **The OpenAPI client is stale.** Run `pnpm generate:api` and ask the user whether to commit the regeneration as a separate PR.
- **You'd need a new dependency.** Stop; ask.
- **A MUI v9 API doesn't behave like the docs you remember.** Stop; check the docs in this repo or fetch the canonical docs.

### Wave 8 — Disaster poller + dispatcher + digests (2h)

**Scope**
- `UsgsEarthquakeSource`, `GdacsSource`, `NhcHurricaneSource` — three `IDataSource` impls.
- `DisasterPoller` BackgroundService: every 5 min, fetch + dedupe + insert.
- Disaster matcher: region filter (country / US state / global), event type filter, severity threshold.
- `Dispatcher` BackgroundService: reads `Match` rows, routes to channels per `AlertChannelMode`.
  - `realtime` — send immediately, **except** when the channel's quiet hours are active → queue and re-attempt at the next allowed moment.
  - `digest-15m` / `digest-hourly` — wait for the next tick.
  - `digest-daily` — wait until the user's chosen hour (default 08:00 local).
- `DigestScheduler` BackgroundService: per (user, mode) tick, builds the digest, sends.
- Channel quiet hours: `Channel.QuietHoursStart` / `QuietHoursEnd` (nullable, local time). UI control on the channel settings.
- `Cleanup` BackgroundService: prune `Event` > 30d, `Notification` > 30d, `AuditLog` > 90d, expired tokens every hour. (Per `1-features.md` resolved decision 5.)

## code-principles.md
# Code Principles

## Core: "Code is not an asset, it is a liability"
The asset is the behavior. Code is the cost. Every line must be read, understood, debugged, updated, and can break.

## Reduction Rules
- Delete unused code — Git has history.
- Delete commented-out code.
- When a feature is superseded, delete old code in the same PR.
- Actively hunt dead code when touching a file.
- Prefer deleting lines over adding lines when behavior stays the same.

## Abstraction & Duplication
- Extract on first duplication (2 call sites = extract).
- Don't add helpers "in case we need them."
- Don't add config options for flexibility — hardcode, add the option when the second use case arrives.

## Error Handling
- Only validate at system boundaries (user input, API responses, DB reads). Trust internal code.
- Don't handle edge cases that can't currently happen — add handling when the case becomes real.

## Comments
- Minimal comments only when completely necessary. Code should be self-explanatory.
- Never comment-out code. Never explain WHAT code does — the code itself should say that.

## Naming
- Named constants over magic numbers/strings, always — even single-use. The name IS the documentation.
- Boolean prefixes: `is`, `has`, `can`, `should` (e.g. `isLoading`, `hasPermission`, `canEdit`).
- Descriptive names for unused params (`_unusedEvent` over `_`).

## Style
- `const`-first — use `let` only when reassignment is needed.
- Early returns / guard clauses — avoid deep nesting.
- Ternary ONLY for simple value assignment (`const x = cond ? a : b`). Everything else uses if/else.
- Direct imports — no barrel files (index.ts re-exports).

## Size Limits
- File: ~800 lines max → refactor is imminent.
- Function/method: ~35 lines max → extract.

## Design
- Apply SOLID and DRY. Use design patterns where they offer utility.

## Folder Architecture ("Use the app → find the code")
The folder tree mirrors UI navigation. Using the app once = knowing where code lives.

```
src/app/
├── pages/           ← one folder per navigable page (flat siblings, no admin/ nesting)
│   └── {page}/
│       ├── {sub-page}/   ← sub-pages as subfolders (e.g. chat/, tasks/)
│       ├── helpers/      ← page-specific services (only used by this page)
│       ├── dialogs/      ← page-specific dialogs
├── services/        ← multi-page services (used by 2+ pages)
│   ├── auth/        ← auth, profile, guards
│   ├── data/        ← firestore facades (user, project, donor...)
│   └── ui/          ← right-panel, dialog-back, mobile-sidebar, title...
├── components/      ← reusable UI (shared components, directives, pipes)
├── models/          ← all interfaces/types grouped by domain (project.model, donor.model...)
```

**Rules:**
- Service used only by its page → `pages/{page}/helpers/`
- Used by 2+ pages → `services/`
- All models in top-level `models/` (dependency arrow: pages → services → models)
- No admin/ grouping — all pages are flat siblings in pages/
- Reusable UI components → `components/`

## mistakes-to-avoid.md
# Mistakes to Avoid

> Feature-specific pitfalls have been moved to the relevant `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files (angular-components, mobile, chat, cloud-functions, testing). Only universal items remain here.

## Behavioral
- **NEVER run recursive PowerShell scripts** like `Get-ChildItem -Recurse | ForEach-Object { Get-Content ... }` — this instantly freezes VS Code. Use `grep_search`, `file_search`, or `read_file` tools instead. Also avoid `Select-String -Recurse` on large trees.
- **E2E tests must show live progress**: Never pipe Playwright output to `Out-String` or use `mode=sync`. Always use `mode=async` so the user sees real-time progress in the terminal.
- **Never hallucinate about external apps.** Say "I don't know" if unsure.
- **Never claim to have "checked the internet"** unless actually fetching a webpage.
- **Ask mobile or desktop first** before debugging layout/alignment issues.
- **Don't auto-update docs** — user confirms via `/update-docs` prompt.
- **Always deploy after code changes** — never leave changes undeployed. Build + `firebase deploy --only hosting --force` immediately after every code edit.
- **Revert failed attempts in the SAME deploy as the fix.**
- **One hypothesis at a time.** Max 3 attempts of the same category — then switch approach.

## E2E / Playwright
- **WebKit CI needs Playwright container**: Use `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble` container for reliable WebKit deps. Standard ubuntu-latest has incomplete WebKit support.
- **WebKit Touch/ContextMenu in mobile emulation**: Playwright's WebKit with iPhone emulation can't construct `Touch()`/`TouchEvent()` (Illegal constructor) and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('contextmenu'))` doesn't trigger Angular bindings. Context menu tests must `test.skip()` on WebKit via `'none'` return from `openMobileContextMenu()`. Real iPhones use native touch — this is a Playwright limitation, not an app bug.
- **Hover action buttons intercepted by adjacent messages**: Fixed via `z-index: 3` on `.message:hover` in `chat.component.scss` — creates stacking context so hover action buttons aren't intercepted by adjacent messages. No `force: true` needed. Must be > 2 (reactions-row z-index) so the emoji picker inside the hovered message stays above other messages' reaction chips.
- **Stacking context traps child z-index values**: When a parent has `z-index` (creating a stacking context), ALL descendants' z-index values are trapped within it. The emoji picker (`z-index: 1000`) inside `.message:hover { z-index: 1 }` was rendered BELOW adjacent reactions (`z-index: 2`) because 1 < 2 in the parent context. Fix: ensure message hover z-index > reactions z-index.
- **`isolation: isolate` causes hover paint loops**: Adding `isolation: isolate` to `main` (grid container) while `.message:hover` toggles z-index creates rapid repaint cycles — the stacking context boundary triggers relayout on each hover frame. Use `position: relative; z-index: 0` on `:host` (app-root) instead for defense-in-depth against CDK overlay competition.
- **Scroll assertions after async operations need polling, not fixed waits**: ResizeObserver + Angular rendering race means `waitForTimeout(500)` is unreliable for scroll position checks. Use `waitForFunction(() => el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight < threshold, null, { timeout: 5000 })`.
- **Scroll-to-bottom button click needs waitForScrollStable**: The button click triggers a `scrollTo` with `behavior: 'smooth'` — measuring `scrollTop` immediately after gives stale values (gap = 8587px instead of <150). Always add `waitForScrollStable()` (RAF-based `scrollTop` convergence check) after programmatic scroll before asserting position.
- **Scroll-to-top in beforeEach needs retry loop**: Real-time Firestore listeners may auto-scroll back to bottom after `scrollTop = 0`. Use a loop that sets `scrollTop = 0`, waits 1s, checks gap, and repeats up to 5 times.
- **@mention popup shows raw UIDs before userNameMap resolves**: Add a `waitForTimeout(500)` before typing filter text, and don't assert on specific user names that depend on async data loading.
- **Textarea highlight overlay jump**: When adding a backdrop div behind a transparent textarea for styled text (e.g. bold mentions), do NOT apply `position: relative; z-index; background: transparent` unconditionally to the textarea — only apply when the overlay is active (e.g. via `.has-mention-overlay` class). Unconditional styles shift the text rendering layout. Also: `overflow: hidden` on the popup container overrides `overflow-y: auto` — so scrolling won't work even if `max-height` is set.

## Testing
- **AngularFire JIT errors in unit tests**: If a spec imports a module that transitively imports `@angular/fire/firestore`, the Angular unit-test builder throws JIT compilation errors. Fix: extract pure functions (e.g. `getLang`, `getLocale`) into a dependency-free file (`active-lang.ts`) and import from there. Don't try `vi.mock` for relative imports — the builder blocks it.
- **Angular test builder blocks `vi.mock` for relative imports**: The `@angular/build:unit-test` vitest-mock-patch rejects `vi.mock('./relative-path')`. Only non-relative module specifiers (`@angular/fire/firestore`, `@angular/fire/auth`, `@shared/time-constants.json`) can be mocked. For services with Angular DI, use `Object.create(Service.prototype)` + manual property assignment to bypass `inject()` calls. Do NOT mock `@angular/core` — `vi.mock("@angular/core", async () => importActual(...))` causes "Cannot access before initialization" errors due to hoisting + async import circular reference.
- **`@shared/*` path alias needs explicit mock**: The `tsconfig.json` alias `@shared/* → functions/shared/*` is resolved by esbuild during Angular test builds. If a transitive import hits `@shared/time-constants.json`, mock it with `vi.mock("@shared/time-constants.json", () => ({ default: { ... } }))` — the factory must return a `default` export since it's a JSON import.

## Firestore Queries
- **Async recompute races with navigation**: `recomputeUnread()` checks `recentlyVisited` at the start, but the async `computeUnreadCount()` call takes a network round-trip. If `handleNavigation()` fires during that gap (zeros count + adds to `recentlyVisited`), the async result overwrites the zero. Fix: re-check `recentlyVisited` AFTER the `await` — not just before. Also: `computeUnreadCount` must subtract the user's own messages (`senderId == uid`) to prevent phantom badges caused by client/server clock drift exceeding `MARK_READ_SKEW_MS`.
- **DM list must use `trackEntity()` like projects/skills**: Manual dual subscriptions (latestMessage$ + readState$) miss the `getActiveId` guard that prevents recomputing unread for the currently-viewed conversation. Always use `UnreadTrackingService.trackEntity()` for all three sections.
- **Collection queries with per-document rules fail for non-privileged users**: A `where("chapterId", "==", X)` query on `projects` is rejected for regular users because Firestore rules require `uid in resource.data.members` — Firestore can't prove the constraint is satisfied without reading every doc. Fix: query with a rule-satisfying constraint (`where("members", "array-contains", uid)`) and filter the other field client-side. Admin/manager can use the direct query.
- **System messages after membership removal fail silently**: If a client posts a system message (via `postSystemMessage` callable) AFTER removing itself from `members[]`, the callable rejects with `permission-denied` (membership check fails). Fix: use a Firestore trigger (`onDocumentWritten`) on the parent doc that detects member array diffs and posts messages server-side with admin privileges. This also eliminates the inverse race (message posted but removal fails → orphaned message).
- **`onSnapshot` cache race disables pagination permanently**: With `includeMetadataChanges: true` + persistent cache, `onSnapshot` emits a stale cache snapshot first (fewer docs than `limitToLast(N)`). If initial-load code sets `hasMoreOlder = (count >= N)` from that cache count, it becomes `false`. The subsequent server snapshot enters steady-state code that never re-evaluates `hasMoreOlder` — user can never scroll-to-load older messages. Fix: (1) use raw snapshot doc count (before client-side `deletedFor` filtering), (2) in steady state, re-enable `hasMoreOlder = true` whenever a snapshot fills the query window (`msgs.length >= PAGE_SIZE`). Affects all chat types equally — more visible in infrequently-visited chats (DMs) where cache is stale.
- **Non-overflowing initial load blocks pagination permanently**: The anchor strategy (`startWithAnchor`) loads only `CONTEXT_SIZE = 10` messages before `lastReadAt`. If those messages are short enough to fit without scrollbar, `scrollHeight <= clientHeight` → the `(scroll)` event never fires → `loadOlderMessages()` never triggers despite `hasMoreOlder === true`. Fix: `loadOlderIfNotOverflowing()` runs after initial render and recursively loads older pages until content overflows or no more exist. Most visible in DMs with short messages.

## Cloud Functions
- **User name resolution must prefer `displayName`**: The `displayName` field is the user's chosen name (set during onboarding — could be a nickname like "Zumi" or a properly formatted full name like "Kovács Nóra" for Hungarian). Never prefer `firstName` — it's just the given name without language-aware ordering. Priority: `displayName` → `firstName` → `'Unknown'`.
- **Rate limit off-by-one pattern**: When a Firestore transaction returns the current count and the outer code checks `current > limit`, the limit is never hit (e.g., limit=5, count reaches 5, `5 > 5` is false). Use `>=` for "at limit" checks after increment-based transactions.
- **Invite-style single-use tokens need transactions**: Any read-then-write pattern where two concurrent callers could both read the "unused" state and both proceed must use `db.runTransaction()`. Without it, both succeed and the last write wins.
- **Find-or-create patterns need deterministic IDs or transactions**: A `findConversation()` → `createConversation()` two-step with auto-generated IDs is a TOCTOU race. Two callers can both see "not found" and both create. Fix: deterministic doc ID (e.g. `uid1_uid2`) + `runTransaction()` on client, or move to a Cloud Function with server-side transaction.
- **Storage triggers must match bucket region**: `onObjectFinalized` must have `{ region: 'us-east1' }` (or whichever region the bucket is in). Mismatched regions cause deploy failure.
- **Speech-to-Text `recognize()` has a 1-minute hard limit**: The synchronous `recognize()` API rejects audio longer than ~60s with `INVALID_ARGUMENT: Sync input too long`. Use `longRunningRecognize()` with a GCS URI (`gs://bucket/path`) for audio estimated >50s. The file must already be in Cloud Storage (which it is for chat attachments).
- **APNs requires explicit priority headers for timely delivery**: Without `'apns-priority': '10'` and `'apns-push-type': 'alert'` in the `apns.headers` block, iOS may classify data-only FCM messages as low-priority background pushes and delay delivery by 10-20+ minutes. Always set both headers when sending visible alert notifications to iOS.
- **`Promise.all` in Firestore triggers must isolate errors**: If one of multiple parallel operations in a trigger throws (e.g. link preview DNS timeout), the entire function fails and Pub/Sub retries with exponential backoff (10s → 20s → 40s...), accumulating to ~19 minutes of delay before the notification finally sends. Wrap each operation with `.catch(e => logger.error(...))` so failures are logged but don't crash the trigger.

## CSS Grid
- **Single-column grid with multiple items targeting same column**: When `grid-template-columns` collapses to `1fr` (e.g. `.no-nav` mode) and multiple items have `grid-column: 1` without explicit `grid-row`, CSS Grid auto-places them into separate rows. Only the first explicit row (`1fr`) gets full height — subsequent implicit rows are `auto`-sized (content height only). Fix: add `grid-row: 1` to the item that needs full height. The mobile breakpoint already had this fix.

## Scroll Anchoring
- **`overflow-anchor: none` on a scroll target causes content-shift drift**: If the user scrolls to an element (e.g. unread separator via `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })`), but that element has `overflow-anchor: none`, the browser picks a *different* element as its scroll anchor (typically the first child below). When content above the separator loads and expands (images, link previews), the browser adjusts scroll to keep the anchor (not the separator) stable — the separator drifts up. Fix: temporarily set `overflow-anchor: auto` on the target element during the grace period. Clear it on user-initiated scroll so normal anchoring resumes. Distinguish programmatic scrolls from user gestures via a brief flag cleared on next rAF.

## Cross-Platform
- **Windows doesn't render flag emojis**: Flag emoji characters (🇬🇧 🇭🇺) display as two-letter country codes on Windows (Edge, Chrome, Firefox). Use inline SVGs for flags instead of emoji. macOS/iOS/Android render them fine.
- **Desktop OS notification toasts truncate after ~3 body lines**: Windows (Action Center) and macOS show only ~3 lines of notification body text. If SW stacking shows more (e.g. 5 visible messages), the OS truncates and the `+N earlier` count doesn't match what's actually readable. Keep `MAX_VISIBLE = 2` so body = "+N earlier" + 2 messages = 3 lines max, fitting the OS toast perfectly.

## Angular / Material
- **`@angular/fire/firestore` `getFirestore()` is lazy/DI-scoped**: On pages that don't inject `Firestore` (e.g. landing page), AngularFire's `getFirestore()` may not return the properly initialized instance. `terminate()` + `clearIndexedDbPersistence()` silently fail (caught by `catch {}`), and the "restart" is just a fast reload without clearing anything. Fix: import from `firebase/firestore` + `firebase/app` directly and use `getFirestore(getApp())` — always returns the real registered instance regardless of Angular DI state.
- **`content-visibility: auto` breaks scroll positioning**: Applying `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-block-size: auto 80px` to chat message bubbles causes scrollbar flickering and incorrect initial scroll position. The `auto` keyword caches rendered size after first paint, but during initial load the estimated 80px doesn't match actual bubble heights (50–400px) — the browser shifts scroll position each time a bubble enters the viewport and gets its real size. Combined with `overflow-anchor: auto`, this creates competing scroll adjustments. Pure CSS "free rendering skip" doesn't work with scroll-to-position-on-load patterns. Use only if messages have fixed known heights.
- **`overflow-anchor` is unreliable for scroll pinning**: Safari/WebKit has ZERO `overflow-anchor` support. Firefox has suppression triggers (adding a class that changes computed properties disables anchoring for that frame). Never rely on CSS `overflow-anchor` alone for critical scroll position maintenance. Use JavaScript: detect drift via `getBoundingClientRect()` comparison and call `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` to re-pin. The `rescrollToSeparator()` pattern checks if the target element drifted >5px from expected position and corrects only when needed — avoids fighting user scroll (content below target loading doesn't cause drift, so no correction fires).
- **Grace period must start immediately in separator path**: If `handleInitialLoad()` sets `firstUnreadMsgId` + `initialScrolledToSeparator` but defers `startScrollGracePeriod()` to a later flush, iOS layout-triggered scroll events fire in between — `handleScroll` sees `isUserNearBottom=true` + `initialScrollGracePeriod=false` and clears `firstUnreadMsgId`. Always start the grace period in the same call that sets the separator state.
- **Deep-unread requires "load around anchor" pattern**: When user has 100+ unread, a single `limitToLast(30)` realtime query loads only the newest 30 (all unread) with no read-boundary context. Fixed with `startWithAnchor(lastReadAt)`: two parallel `getDocs` (context `endAt(lastReadAt) + limitToLast(10)` + unread `startAfter(lastReadAt) + limit(30)`), merged and deduplicated by ID, sorted by timestamp. A tail realtime listener (`startAfter(newestLoadedTs)`) then handles new messages. No backfill loop needed.
- **Read receipts render async and shift bottom position**: `readState` subscription arrives after initial `scrollToBottom()` fires. The ~17px (16px avatar + 1px padding) of read receipt avatars below the last message pushes the previous "bottom" above the viewport. Fix: in the `onUpdate` callback from `ChatReadReceiptService`, call `scrollToBottom()` during the initial scroll grace period when user is near bottom. `overflow-anchor: auto` alone doesn't fix this because the anchor is a message above — the new content appears below the anchor.
- **iOS Safari doesn't reliably fire `contextmenu` on long-press**: The native `contextmenu` DOM event is unreliable on iOS — especially when elements contain `<img>` tags (triggers native image callout) or use CDK drag-drop with competing touch delays. Fix: use `LongPressDirective` (`appLongPress`) which dispatches a synthetic `contextmenu` MouseEvent after 500ms touch-hold. All list rows using `ContextMenuHelper` + `(contextmenu)` must also have `appLongPress`. The directive adds `-webkit-touch-callout: none` and runs listeners outside Angular zone. Also add `pointer-events: none` on `<img>` elements inside list rows to prevent them from stealing the gesture.
- **Chrome Mobile `setSelectionRange` throws DOMException "illegal access"**: On Android Chrome (especially older versions like Android 10), calling `textarea.setSelectionRange()` on an unfocused element throws a DOMException. Wrap all `setSelectionRange` calls in a `safeSetSelectionRange(el, start, end)` helper that catches and silently ignores the error. The cursor position is cosmetic — losing it is acceptable.
- **Firestore real-time arrays can contain `undefined` entries**: During network instability or cache corruption, `collectionData()` can emit arrays with undefined items. Defensive `filter(Boolean)` should be applied at the data-layer level (`FirestoreRepository.allDocs$()`, shared data services) — not just at subscription sites.
- **`Notification.requestPermission()` must be first await on mobile**: Mobile browsers (especially Chrome Android) require `Notification.requestPermission()` to be called in the same synchronous microtask as the user's tap. Any `await` before it (e.g. `await waitForInit()`) breaks the user-activation chain — the browser silently ignores the permission prompt with no dialog, no error.
- **PWA manifest `"orientation"` doesn't lock on Android Chrome**: The `"orientation": "portrait"` field in `manifest.webmanifest` is a hint that Chrome ignores for installed PWAs. Must call `screen.orientation.lock('portrait')` programmatically when `display-mode: standalone` matches. Use `(screen.orientation as any)?.lock?.()` — TypeScript's `ScreenOrientation` type doesn't include `lock`.
- **`-webkit-user-select` needed on mobile**: Android Chrome requires the `-webkit-` prefix for `user-select: none` to work. Always set both: `-webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none;`. Restore `user-select: text` (with prefix) on `input`/`textarea` elements.
- **`blurOnKeyboardClose()` needs growth threshold + focus grace period on iOS**: The `visualViewport.resize` handler that blurs inputs when the keyboard closes must check for significant height growth (>100px), not any growth. On iOS Safari, the autocorrect/predictive text bar and `100dvh` recalculations cause small viewport height fluctuations during normal typing. Without a threshold, every keystroke triggers blur → keyboard dismiss → reopen cycle. Typical keyboard height is 250–350px, so 100px threshold safely distinguishes toolbar adjustments from full keyboard close. Additionally: a 600ms grace period after `focusin` is required — iOS sends transient positive viewport deltas during keyboard *open* animation that exceed 100px and would trigger blur.
- **iOS WebKit resigns first responder on sibling programmatic scroll**: On iOS Safari, calling `scrollTop = N` or `scrollTo()` on a sibling element while the keyboard is animating open causes WebKit to blur the focused textarea — the keyboard appears then immediately dismisses. Fix: skip all programmatic scroll adjustments in viewport resize handlers when `document.activeElement` is an input/textarea. The scroll will correct itself naturally once the keyboard finishes animating.
- **ResizeObserver + keyboard = cumulative scroll drift**: A `ResizeObserver` that applies `scrollTop += delta` to compensate for container height changes (e.g. top bar appearing) will mis-adjust during keyboard open/close — the container shrinks/grows from the **bottom** (via `100dvh` chain), not the top. Height-comparison detection races with `visualViewport` resize handler. Fix: use a `viewportResizing` boolean flag set by `visualViewport` resize handler (cleared 400ms after last event). ResizeObserver checks the flag and skips delta during keyboard animation.
- **iOS video thumbnails need `playsinline` + no `opacity: 0` fade-in**: iOS Safari ignores `preload="metadata"` on `<video>` elements, so `loadeddata` never fires. If CSS starts video at `opacity: 0` waiting for a `.loaded` class, the thumbnail stays invisible. Fix: always add `playsinline` attribute to inline `<video>` elements, and don't use `opacity: 0` → `.loaded { opacity: 1 }` on videos — show them immediately with a dark background fallback. Images can keep fade-in.
- **OnPush `uiTick` must propagate through ALL component layers**: If `ChatComponent` (Default CD) passes `[uiTick]` to `MessageBubbleComponent` (OnPush), but `MessageBubbleComponent` doesn't forward it to `TextBubbleComponent` (also OnPush), the inner component NEVER re-checks when `uiTick` changes — its inputs (`msg`, `host`) are the same references. Always chain `[uiTick]` through every OnPush layer that reads host state (like `host.getReadReceipts()`). Symptom: "seen" avatars take 60+ seconds to appear (waiting for unrelated CD trigger).
- **Race between `readState` subscription and `userNameMap$`**: The readState `collectionData` listener and the `users$` collection listener are independent Firestore queries. If readState arrives first, `userNameMap` is empty → avatars have no `photoURL`. Must call `refreshNames()` (rebuild readStates from rawReadStates) when userNameMap/userPhotoMap update, plus `tickAndDetect()` to push to OnPush children.
- **Production minification strips `if (!x) return` guards**: Angular's production optimizer can remove null-check early-return guards in component methods if the template types suggest null isn't possible. Use **optional chaining** (`task?.createdBy`) instead — `?.` compiles to a null-check that minifiers cannot strip.
- **`MatNativeDateModule` in standalone components**: Don't import `MatNativeDateModule` — it doesn't reliably provide `DateAdapter` in standalone components after tree-shaking. Use `provideNativeDateAdapter()` in `providers` instead. All datepicker components must follow this pattern.
- **Bare text in `<mat-form-field>`**: Never use bare `{{ ... | transloco }}` for labels or errors inside `<mat-form-field>`. Wrap labels in `<mat-label>`, errors in `<mat-error>` — bare interpolation renders as unstyled inline text that doesn't float or style as errors. `floatLabel: "always"` has no effect without `<mat-label>`.
- **CSS stacking: `position: relative` sibling paints over `static` sibling**: A `position: relative` element paints above a `position: static` sibling, regardless of DOM order. In chat, `.message` had `position: relative` (for hover z-index) and `.read-receipts` was `static` — the bubble painted over the receipt avatars. Fix: add `position: relative` to `.read-receipts` so DOM order determines paint order. General rule: if two siblings overlap (negative margins, absolute children), ensure both have the same `position` type.
- **Fixed `CHARS_PER_LINE` in bubble collapse clips mobile messages**: `ChatBubbleCollapseService` estimated wrapping with a hardcoded 50 chars/line. On mobile, bubbles are ~255px wide (68% of 375px) and fit only ~25 chars/line — the service underestimated line count, didn't trigger "see more", and CSS `overflow-y: clip` silently truncated content. Fix: compute `charsPerLine` dynamically from `window.innerWidth * 0.68 - padding`, capped at 50 for desktop.
- **`overflow-y: clip` + fixed `max-height` clips variable-height content**: `.bubble-content` uses `overflow-y: clip` + `max-height` for collapse animation. When a link preview image or reply quote consumes part of the pixel budget, the "see more" link and text below get silently clipped. Fix: `getMaxHeight(msg)` returns `null` (no CSS max-height) for messages with `linkPreview` or `replyTo` — rely solely on `getTruncatedText` for content limiting.
- **`FIELD_VALIDATORS` includes `required` for location**: The shared `FIELD_VALIDATORS["location"]` preset includes `Validators.required`. Pages where location is optional (e.g. profile page, admin user-edit page) must NOT use this preset — use `[Validators.maxLength(100)]` directly. A required validator on an optional field makes the form permanently invalid, silently blocking ALL autosave operations (skills, contacts, off-periods, etc.).
- **`mat-icon-button` as `matIconSuffix` adds height to form fields**: A `<button mat-icon-button matIconSuffix>` adds 48px height, making the field taller than adjacent fields using `mat-datepicker-toggle`. Use `<mat-icon matIconSuffix>` instead for compact icons. Put `(click)` on the `<mat-form-field>` so clicking anywhere opens the picker.
- **Flexbox `align-items: stretch` makes siblings match tallest sibling**: When a date field has `<mat-hint>` but the adjacent time field doesn't, the time field stretches to the same height. Fix: `align-items: flex-start` on the flex container.
- **Drag-then-click in custom scroll wheels**: A `click` event fires after `mouseup` even when the user was dragging. If the wheel has both drag and click-to-select handlers, the click overrides the drag result. Fix: track `wasDragged` (set when movement > 3px), suppress click handler when true.
- **Don't rely on routing-class CSS for layout-critical overflow**: Classes set via `NavigationEnd` (e.g. `admin-center-active` on `<main>`) arrive after the component DOM renders. During hard reset, there's a window where the page is rendered but the class isn't applied — touch input during this gap scrolls `.grid-content` and the scrollTop gets stuck when `:host { overflow: hidden }` later takes effect. Use `:host` styles on the component instead (timing-independent).
- **Scroll chaining on mobile internal lists**: When a scrolling list (e.g. `.invite-list`) reaches its end, continued swiping chains to the parent and scrolls away headers/toolbars. Add `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the list container.
- **Admin-center list bottom clipping by bottom nav**: `<main>` has `padding-bottom: var(--hm-bottom-nav-height)` on mobile, but admin-center pages set it to `0` because the padding must live on the internal list container — otherwise there's dead space between the list and the bottom nav.

- **CDK 21 Popover API renders overlays in top layer — z-index can't compete**: Angular CDK 21 uses `popover="manual"` + `showPopover()` for overlay hosts, promoting them to the browser's top layer. No z-index on a regular body-level element (like `.pac-container`) can appear above top-layer elements. - **Close popups/pickers BEFORE `await`**: When a button click triggers an async Firestore write and also dismisses a popup, set the visibility flag to `null`/`false` BEFORE the `await` — not after. Otherwise the popup stays open for the entire network round-trip (feels unresponsive, hover-leave doesn't dismiss because `showEmojiPickerForMsg` keeps the element rendered). Pattern: `this.showPicker = null; await this.doWrite();`.
- **Deleting IndexedDB while Firestore has active listeners crashes SDK**: `indexedDB.deleteDatabase()` on Firestore's persistence DB triggers "Firestore shutting down" error. Always `terminate(firestore)` + `clearIndexedDbPersistence(firestore)` (Firebase's own API) before clearing caches. Add a safety timeout (`setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 3000)`) in case `terminate` hangs (e.g. blocked by another tab). `clearIndexedDbPersistence` must only be called on a terminated instance.

## Build / Deploy
- **Always `npx tsc` in `functions/`** before deploying Cloud Functions. No predeploy hook.
- **PowerShell**: Quote comma-separated firebase targets: `firebase deploy --only "functions,hosting"`.
- **Always use `--force`** on `firebase deploy` to skip interactive confirmation prompts (e.g. "Would you like to proceed?" when creating new functions). Never let deploy commands hang waiting for input.
- **Deploy storage rules alongside hosting**: `firebase deploy --only hosting` does NOT deploy `storage.rules`. If storage paths were added/changed, always `firebase deploy --only "storage,hosting"`.
- **Storage `allow write` blocks deletes**: `allow write` with `request.resource.size`/`contentType` checks fails for `delete` operations (where `request.resource` is null). Always split into `allow create, update` + separate `allow delete`.
- **JSON imports outside `include` expand `rootDir`**: Fix: set explicit `"rootDir": "."` in tsconfig.
- **CI/CD Firebase Functions IAM**: Service account needs Cloud Functions Developer, Service Account User, Secret Manager Secret Accessor + Viewer, Cloud Scheduler Admin.
- **GCP quota throttling**: When deploying 60+ functions, some may fail. Redeploy failed ones individually.

## Encoding
- **NO BOM in JSON files**: Browsers/Transloco interpret BOM bytes as content → mojibake.
- **Never use PowerShell `Out-File`/`Set-Content` for UTF-8 with diacritics** — use Node.js `fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync`.

## Firebase Auth
- **`authDomain` must match hosting domain** (`web.app`, not `firebaseapp.com`).
- **In-app browsers block all OAuth flows**: Detect via UA regex, show "Open in browser" UI.
- **`intent://` is Android-only**: On iOS, show "Copy link" with Safari instructions.
- **Capacitor Google Auth `server_client_id` must be web client ID**: In `android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`, `server_client_id` must be the **web** OAuth client (type 3), not an Android client (type 1). Using Android client ID causes DEVELOPER_ERROR code=10. The `capacitor.config.ts` `serverClientId` and `strings.xml` must match the same web client ID.

## Capacitor / Native Android
- **Toolbar clipped by status bar on native**: With `viewport-fit=cover` + Capacitor `androidScheme: 'https'`, the WebView renders edge-to-edge. The toolbar needs `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` and height must be `calc(base-height + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px))`. On regular web/PWA, `env(safe-area-inset-top)` resolves to `0px` (no change).
- **Bottom content clipped by gesture nav bar**: Edge-to-edge means the WebView extends behind the Android gesture bar (or 3-button nav bar). `--hm-bottom-nav-height` MUST include `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` — defined as `calc(56px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`. Without it, every scrollable list's last item and every `position: fixed; bottom: 0` element gets clipped. Checklist for new fixed-bottom elements: add `padding-bottom: max(Npx, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`. For scrollable page bodies on admin-center routes: add `padding-bottom: var(--hm-bottom-nav-height)` in `@include bp.mobile`. For fullscreen overlays (sidebar overlays): add `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)`. Material dialogs (bottom-sheet on mobile) get it via global `.mat-mdc-dialog-surface` rule.
- **Google profile photo images broken in Capacitor WebView**: Capacitor's origin is `https://localhost` — Google CDN (`lh3.googleusercontent.com`) may reject requests with this as referrer. Fix: `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">` globally in `index.html`. Also add `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` on individual `<img>` tags as defense-in-depth. Does not break Firebase SDK (uses authenticated tokens, not referrer-based auth).

## SEO / Crawlers
- **SPA catch-all rewrite breaks `robots.txt`**: Firebase Hosting's `"source": "**", "destination": "/index.html"` rewrite serves index.html for `/robots.txt` if no static file exists. Always include `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` as static assets in `angular.json`. Firebase serves static files before rewrites.
- **Static crawler fallback needs CSS hiding, not inline `<script>`**: An inline `<script>` placed before the fallback `<div>` in DOM order can't query it (not yet parsed). Even when placed after, there's still a paint-before-execute flash. Fix: use `<style>[data-crawler-fallback]{display:none!important}</style>` in `<head>` + `<noscript><style>` override to `display:flex`. Zero flash, crawlers still see content.


## Dark Theme / CSS
- **`ViewEncapsulation.None` breaks `:host-context()`**: Chat component uses `None` — `:host-context(.dark-theme)` emits literal CSS browsers ignore outside Shadow DOM. Use `.dark-theme app-chat { ... }` instead.
- **Add `!important` to dark overrides** when original styles are deeply nested (specificity wins).

[Authorize(Policy = Permissions.ChannelsReadOwn)]
[ProducesResponseType(typeof(IReadOnlyList<ChannelResponse>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
public async Task<ActionResult<IReadOnlyList<ChannelResponse>>> ListAsync(CancellationToken ct)

    if (currentUser.Id is not { } userId) return Unauthorized();
    var rows = await db.Channels

- Next.js 16 App Router. React 19. TypeScript **strict**. MUI v9.
- TanStack Query v5 for client state. React Hook Form + Zod for forms.
- No Tailwind. No shadcn. No Chakra. **MUI only.**
- **Default to Server Components.** Add `'use client'` only when the component needs state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs, or third-party client-only libraries.
- **Push `'use client'` to the leaf.** A wrapper with state, a `<form>` that uses `useForm`, a button with `(onClick)`. Don't mark a whole page client-side just because one child needs it.

- **Never import server-only modules from a client component.** `fs`, `path`, `next/headers`, `next/cookies`, server-only secrets, etc. are off-limits on the client. Use the `server-only` package to make this a build error.
- **Data fetching**: Server Components fetch directly. Client components use `useQuery`. Don't mix the two (Server Component fetches, then passes data to a Client Component via props).
- **`sx` prop for dynamic styles.** `style={{}}` is forbidden when the value is computed at runtime.
- **Theme tokens, not hard-coded values.** `theme.spacing(2)`, `theme.palette.primary.main`, never `'#1976d2'` or `'16px'` in component code.
- **One `<ThemeProvider>` at the root** of `(app)`, `(admin)`, and `(auth)` route groups. Don't nest.
- **No inline `style={{}}` with static values** — use `sx` consistently.
- **`useTheme()` is fine**; reading `theme` from context in the same component is preferred over passing it down.
- **Iconify or `@mui/icons-material`** for icons. Don't import random SVG files.
- React Hook Form + Zod schema, colocated. Schema lives next to the form, e.g. `SignUpForm.tsx` + `signUpSchema.ts`.
- **One Zod schema per form.** Reuse via `z.infer<typeof schema>` for the form's input/output types.
- **Server errors come back typed.** Map the API's `ProblemDetails` (RFC 7807) to a Zod issue, display with `<FormHelperText error>`.
- **No `defaultValues` from props without memoization.** Pass them through `useMemo` or use `values` from a parent query.
- **Query keys are tuples, hierarchical**: `['alerts', alertId, 'history']`. Invalidation: `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['alerts'] })`.
- **No `refetchOnWindowFocus` globally off** unless the data is large and stale is fine. Default is on.
- **Mutations invalidate the smallest set of queries possible.** Don't blast `['alerts']` if you only need `['alerts', alertId]`.
- **Loading states are explicit.** `if (isPending) return <Skeleton />`. No spinners unless the operation is user-initiated.
- **Error states are explicit.** Render `<Alert severity="error">` with a retry button. Never `console.error` and render `null`.
- Access token in memory (Zustand or React context). Refresh token in an httpOnly cookie (set by the backend).
- **`fetch` wrapper intercepts 401 once**, calls `/auth/refresh`, retries the original request. If refresh fails, redirect to sign-in.
- `pnpm --dir web generate:api` regenerates types from the backend's Swagger doc. Run this on every backend change.
- **The client is committed.** Drift is a build error in CI (a separate job compares the committed client to a fresh regeneration and fails if they differ).
- **Use `openapi-fetch` for requests, not raw `fetch`.** Types come for free.
- **Named exports only.** No `export default`. Components, hooks, utilities — all named.
- **No `useEffect` for data fetching.** Use `useQuery`. `useEffect` is for side effects on prop changes (rare).
- **No `useMemo` / `useCallback` "just in case".** Only when there's a measured or obvious reason.
- **No barrel files** (`index.ts` re-exports). Direct imports: `import { Foo } from '@/features/alerts/Foo'`.
- **File size**: ~300 lines max. Extract when approaching the limit.
- Vitest + Testing Library for unit. Playwright for e2e.
- **Test behavior, not implementation.** Don't assert internal state; assert the rendered output or the API call.
- **No real network in unit tests.** Use `msw` to mock the OpenAPI client.
- **No real time** without a controllable clock. Use `vi.useFakeTimers()`.
- Every form input has a `<label>` (use MUI's `<TextField label="…">`).
- Every interactive element is keyboard-reachable in document order.
- Color contrast meets WCAG AA (the default MUI theme does).

- `// @ts-ignore` (use `// @ts-expect-error` with a reason, or fix the type)
- Tailwind, shadcn, Chakra, or any UI library other than MUI

modeInstructions.content:
# Frontend Reviewer

You review frontend changes for **Sonrisa News** in Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript + MUI v9. You are read-only.

## Mandate

Given a diff, produce a structured review covering:

1. **Accessibility (a11y)**
2. **MUI usage**
3. **Server / Client boundary**
4. **React Server Components (RSC)**
5. **Error boundaries and loading states**
6. **OpenAPI client drift**
7. **State management (React Query)**
8. **Forms (React Hook Form + Zod)**
9. **Style / consistency**

You check the rules in `.github/instructions/nextjs-react.instructions.md`.

## Output format

```
## Review of <files or PR>

### Critical (blocks merge)
- [CRITICAL] <file>:<line> — <what's wrong, why it matters, what to do>

### Should fix (not blocking)
- [SHOULD] <file>:<line> — <what's wrong, what to do>

### Nit (optional)
- [NIT] <file>:<line> — <what's wrong, what to do>

### Praises
- <What was done well — call out the good patterns>

### Summary
- <One sentence: approve / request changes / comment>
```

## Checklists

### A11y

- [ ] Every form input has a `<label>` (MUI `<TextField label="…">` is the usual)
- [ ] Every icon-only button has `aria-label`
- [ ] Every interactive element is keyboard-reachable
- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG AA (default MUI theme does)
- [ ] No `div` as a button
- [ ] Focus is managed when modals open / close
- [ ] Headings follow a logical hierarchy

### MUI usage

- [ ] `sx` prop for dynamic styles (no inline `style={{}}` with computed values)
- [ ] Theme tokens, not hard-coded values (`theme.spacing(2)`, not `'16px'`)
- [ ] No inline `style={{}}` with static values either (use `sx`)
- [ ] One `<ThemeProvider>` at the root of each route group
- [ ] Icons come from `@mui/icons-material` or Iconify, not random SVGs
- [ ] No `makeStyles` (deprecated in v9)

### Server / Client boundary

- [ ] Default to Server Components. `'use client'` is at the leaf.
- [ ] No server-only modules imported from a client component
- [ ] `useState`, `useEffect`, `useReducer`, event handlers → client component
- [ ] Data fetching: Server Components fetch directly; client components use `useQuery`
- [ ] No `'use client'` on a page component (push it to a child)
- [ ] No `next/headers` or `next/cookies` in a client component

### RSC pitfalls

- [ ] No `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, or `new Date()` in a Server Component that affects render (causes hydration mismatches)
- [ ] No browser-only API (`window`, `document`, `localStorage`) in a Server Component
- [ ] `useSearchParams()` wrapped in `<Suspense>` (Next.js 16 requirement)
- [ ] `cookies()` and `headers()` are awaited (Next.js 16 async dynamic APIs)
- [ ] No `useState` in a Server Component

### Error boundaries and loading states

- [ ] Every page-level route has a `loading.tsx`
- [ ] Every page-level route has an `error.tsx`
- [ ] Forms have explicit error UI (not `console.error` + `null`)
- [ ] Loading states are skeletons, not spinners, unless the operation is user-initiated
- [ ] `useQuery` failures render `<Alert severity="error">` with a retry button

### OpenAPI client drift

- [ ] The diff doesn't import a type that isn't in the generated client
- [ ] The diff doesn't change the OpenAPI doc without regenerating the client
- [ ] The frontend doesn't construct URLs by hand (`/api/v1/...`) — it uses the client's methods
- [ ] The `useQuery` / `useMutation` uses the typed client, not raw `fetch`

### React Query

- [ ] Query keys are tuples, hierarchical
- [ ] Mutations invalidate the smallest set of queries possible
- [ ] `staleTime` is set when the data is large or slow to refetch
- [ ] No `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` without a reason
- [ ] No `enabled: false` that should be `'loading'` UI

### Forms (React Hook Form + Zod)

- [ ] Zod schema colocated with the form
- [ ] Server errors mapped to Zod issues (or to a form-level error)
- [ ] `defaultValues` are memoized if computed from props
- [ ] `mode: 'onBlur'` or `'onChange'` set, not the default
- [ ] Submit button is `disabled` while `isSubmitting`

## Tone

- Direct. Not preachy.
- Specific. `"src/app/(app)/alerts/page.tsx:23 — `style={{ marginTop: 16 }}` should be `sx={{ mt: 2 }}`"`
- Not a stickler for trivial style. The user can fix nits in a follow-up.

## When to escalate

- **The diff breaks the build.** Say "this won't build, fix and resubmit" up front.
- **The diff introduces a new UI library, even partially.** Stop and tell the user.
- **The diff changes the OpenAPI client regeneration.** A separate PR is the convention.
- **You find an a11y issue that blocks a screen reader user.** Critical, not a nit.

## Review of Wave 5 Frontend — `features/alerts/*`, `app/(app)/alerts/[id]`, `features/channels/AddChannelDialog`

### Critical (blocks merge)

- [CRITICAL] `web/features/alerts/useAlertsQueries.ts:54` — `useAlertChannelModesQuery(alertId)` uses `enabled: alertId.length > 0`, but every other consumer of this hook (notably `AlertDetail`) currently fetches the **full** alert list (`useAlertsQuery`) and then resolves the single alert client-side. When the user navigates to `/alerts/{id}` for an alert that exists on the server but hasn't been fetched yet (cold cache, hard refresh on a shared URL), `useAlertChannelModesQuery` is enabled against an `alertId` that *does* exist, so this guard is fine — **but** the more important problem is that the matrix page never refetches the channels list when the user adds a new channel from inside an alert's detail page. The `onChannelCreated` callback in `AddChannelDialog` is a `() => void` that just closes the dialog; the `useChannelsQuery` in `AlertDetail` is unaware. **Fix:** pass the new channel id back via `onChannelCreated(channelId)` and call `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["channels"] })` from the parent's `onChannelCreated` handler. (See NIT-2 in `wave4-frontend-followup.md` — the signature is already correct in `AddChannelDialog`, the `AddChannelButton` was just updated to swallow the id.)

- [CRITICAL] `web/app/(app)/alerts/[id]/page.tsx:28` — When the user navigates directly to `/alerts/{id}` for an alert they own, the page fetches the **entire** alert list and filters client-side. That's fine for the MVP, but the page also has a hard `<Typography variant="body2">` "Channel-mode matrix" without a real heading hierarchy — the `<h2>` is the alert name in `AlertDetail`, but it's a `Typography variant="h5" component="h2"` rather than `h1`. The page is missing an `h1` for the alert title at the page level (the breadcrumb is the only thing above the `h2`). **Fix:** add an `h1` (the alert name) at the top of the page; downscale the `h2` in `AlertDetail` to `h3`. Screen readers expect one `h1` per page.

- [CRITICAL] `web/features/alerts/ChannelModeMatrix.tsx:48-110` — The `<Select>` is rendered with `value={value}` where `value: DeliveryMode | ""`. The empty string is the "Don't deliver" sentinel, but **the actual mode value can also be the empty string when the row is missing** (no row in `modes` for this `(alertId, channelId)` pair). When the user opens the dropdown, sees "Don't deliver" highlighted as the current selection, and picks it, the `onChange` fires with `""` and the matrix calls `onChange(channel.Id, null)` — but if the row is already missing, the `removeChannelMode` mutation is a no-op (the controller returns 404). Not blocking, but the cell **should not** treat missing-row == explicit-don't-deliver, because once a future refactor makes the controller idempotent on 404, the user clicks do nothing. **Fix:** track an explicit "not set" sentinel different from `""` (e.g. `value: DeliveryMode | undefined`) and only call `removeChannelMode` when the previous value was a real mode.

### Should fix (not blocking)

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertEditorDialog.tsx:131-145` — When the backend returns `ValidationError` with multiple field errors, the dialog maps only the first message per field to `fieldErrors` and the rest to a single generic inline `<Alert>`. The form would be clearer if the per-field `helperText` reflected all backend errors (e.g. `fieldErrors["symbols"] = ["Add at least one symbol", "Symbols must be uppercase"]`). Low-cost improvement.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertList.tsx:108-110` — The "New alert" button on the empty state is the *only* way to create an alert when the list is empty, but the button in the page header (at the top of the page in `(app)/alerts/page.tsx`) is currently the `AddChannelButton`. The empty state hides the "New alert" affordance if the user has channels but no alerts, because the empty state is for "no alerts at all". **Fix:** also surface a "New alert" button in the page header alongside the "Add Channel" button, or merge both into a single `AddMenu` with two items. The current UX forces a new user to find the empty state before discovering the create affordance.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertList.tsx:189-199` — The alert card renders the alert name as a `<Typography component={Link}>`, but the surrounding `<Card>` has no `onClick` and the "Edit" button is in `<CardActions>`. Keyboard users can tab to the name link, but **the Edit / Test / Delete buttons are after the link, before the Switch in the same row** — and the Switch's `inputProps` are at `slotProps.input` (correctly converted from `inputProps` per MUI v9), but the Switch sits between the name link and the action buttons. Tab order: name link → Switch → Edit → Test → Delete. That's fine, but the name link and the row's actions live in two different `<Stack>` blocks, so a screen reader user landing on the name link hears "Your alert" + "Channel-mode matrix" and then the actions, with no implicit grouping. **Fix:** wrap the whole row in a `<Card role="article" aria-labelledby={`alert-${alert.Id}`}>` and put the name in a `<Typography id={`alert-${alert.Id}`}>`. (Or accept the NIT and move on.)

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/ChannelModeMatrix.tsx:88-90` — `inputProps` on `<Select>` is removed in MUI v9 (you used `slotProps.input` on `<Switch>` correctly, but missed this one). TypeScript currently allows it because it's a pass-through to the underlying `<input>`, but the typed name has moved. **Fix:** replace with `slotProps={{ input: { "aria-label": ... } }}` for consistency with the Switch and to avoid a deprecation warning when MUI ships v10.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertDetail.tsx:96-105` — When `channelsQuery` succeeds but returns an empty list, the matrix is hidden behind an `<Alert severity="info">` that has a "Channel-mode matrix" heading two lines above it. Good. But the "Currently set: …" caption below the matrix displays the channel id prefix (`m.ChannelId.slice(0, 8)`) instead of the channel destination. **Fix:** look up the channel by id from the `channels` prop and display the destination (or type) instead of the GUID prefix. A user looking at the caption cannot tell which row is which.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/api.ts:18` — `ValidationError` is thrown from the mutations, but the type guard inside `unwrap` matches on `kind === "validation"` only for status 400. The backend's alert controller also returns 400 with a non-`ValidationProblemDetails` body for some input errors (e.g. the `RejectEmptyGuid` 400). The `unwrap` would fall through to `kind: "http"` and the mutation would throw a generic `Error`, losing the field-level UX. **Fix:** check for a `400` with *any* `errors`-shaped body, not just `response.status === 400`. (Or, on the backend, always return `ValidationProblemDetails` for `400`.)

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertEditorDialog.tsx:148` — The `<input type="checkbox">` rendered for the "Enabled" switch is a raw HTML element, not the MUI `<Checkbox>`. Inconsistent with the `<Switch>` in `AlertList`. **Fix:** use `<Checkbox checked={enabled} onChange={...} />` for visual consistency.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertList.tsx:208` — `handleToggleEnabled` is `(_: unknown, checked: boolean)` but the actual `<Switch onChange>` handler in MUI v9 passes `(event, checked: boolean)`. The `_: unknown` is fine, but the checked value should be `event.target.checked` for safety. The current code works because the second positional arg is correct; just be explicit.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/channels/AddChannelDialog.tsx:90` — `setChannelId(channel.Id)` is still called, but the new `startVerifyMutation.mutate({ channelId: newId })` reads the value from the variable. The `setChannelId` is now only used by the `confirmVerify` step (which reads it from state). The mutation's closure pattern is correct, but a comment in the code explains the old `setChannelId`+`mutate()` interleaving and the new code does not — that comment block was useful context. **Fix:** add a one-line comment: "setChannelId is the sentinel for the confirmVerify step (state-read); startVerify reads its id from the variable, not from state (see NIT-3)."

- [SHOULD] `web/features/channels/AddChannelDialog.tsx:60-75` — The `DialogError` discriminated union is correct, but the `kind` field is duplicated work at every call site (`setError({ kind: "validation", message: ... })` 7 places). Consider exporting the constructors: `const validationError = (m: string) => ({ kind: "validation" as const, message: m })` and `apiError(m)`. Reduces typo risk.

- [SHOULD] `web/features/alerts/AlertList.tsx:108` — `<EmptyState>` renders a `<Card variant="outlined"><CardContent>` but the rest of the list uses `<Card variant="outlined">` consistently. The empty state is fine, but the **header row** (the alert-type `<Typography variant="h6">` like "News") is rendered even when the group is empty. The `if (rows === undefined || rows.length === 0) return null;` guard is correct, but the **`alertTypeOrder.map`** still iterates all 3 types when only one has rows. With 3 types, the cost is negligible; with more, the constant overhead grows. **Fix:** if the data is small, accept it. Otherwise, build a `<Set>` of types present in `data` and iterate that.

### Nit (optional)

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/AlertFilterFields.tsx:51-60` — `updateFilters` is a free function that re-stringifies JSON. The same logic appears in all three sub-forms. **Fix:** extract a `useFiltersState` hook. (But three call sites is the threshold, not two — see the user memory: "Extract on first duplication (2 call sites = extract).")

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/api.ts:71-73` — `deleteAlert` returns `Promise<ApiResult<null>>` but `null` is a poor type — the API returns 204 No Content with no body. **Fix:** use `Promise<ApiResult<void>>`.

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/AlertEditorDialog.tsx:155-160` — The `<input type="checkbox">` is wrapped in a `<FormControlLabel>` with the label as a string. The `onChange` handler is `(e) => setEnabled(e.target.checked)`. The label is descriptive enough; the raw `<input>` is invisible. **Fix:** use `<Checkbox ... />` from MUI for visual + a11y consistency.

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/ChannelModeMatrix.tsx:31-33` — `cellId` is defined but never used. Dead code. **Fix:** delete.

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/filterSchemas.ts:96-100` — The compile-time guard (`const _exhaustive: Record<AlertType, unknown> = ...; void _exhaustive;`) is defensive but is satisfied by the `filterSchemaByType` and `filterSchemaFor` maps already. The `_exhaustive` and `ALERT_TYPES` reference at the bottom of the file is dead code. **Fix:** delete both lines.

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/useAlertsQueries.ts:189-200` — `MatcherNotWiredError` is a custom class. So is `ValidationError`. The two are siblings. Consider a small `errors.ts` module to hold them. (Acceptable inline for now; extract when a third error class lands.)

- [NIT] `web/features/channels/AddChannelDialog.tsx:179-181` — The "autoFocus on mount" comment from NIT-5 of the wave 4 followup is still missing. Add the one-line comment for the future reader.

- [NIT] `web/features/alerts/AlertList.tsx:140-150` — `groupByType` returns a `Map<AlertType, AlertResponse[]>`. The `.get` chain is fine, but TypeScript narrows poorly because the map is mutable. A `Record<AlertType, AlertResponse[]>` would narrow better. **Fix:** switch to `Record<AlertType, AlertResponse[]>`.

### Praises

- **OpenAPI-first.** The `api.ts` wrappers are tiny, return a discriminated `ApiResult` union so callers don't need to know `openapi-fetch`'s shape, and surface `ValidationProblemDetails` as a typed `ValidationError` exception. The `useTestAlertMutation` catches the wave-6 501 as a typed `MatcherNotWiredError` and the dialog handles it gracefully. This is the right shape for the rest of the project.
- **Filter schemas match the backend's DTOs.** The Zod schemas in `filterSchemas.ts` mirror `NewsAlertFilters.cs` / `MarketAlertFilters.cs` / `DisasterAlertFilters.cs` (strict — unknown properties are rejected). The round-trip through `canonicalize` keeps the column shape consistent.
- **Hierarchical query keys.** `['alerts']` / `['alerts', id]` / `['alerts', id, 'channels']` / `['channels']` — and mutations invalidate the smallest set. `setChannelMode` only invalidates the modes for *that* alert, not the whole list.
- **ChannelModeMatrix as a controlled component.** The matrix takes `onChange(channelId, mode | null)` and the parent owns the mutation. The matrix is testable in isolation (no React Query) and the test will be straightforward.
- **AddChannelDialog refactor.** NITs 1, 2, 3, 9 from the wave 4 followup handoff are correctly addressed — the `DialogError` discriminated union, the new `onChannelCreated(channelId)` signature, and the `{ channelId, code }` variable pattern for the confirm mutation. The fragile `setChannelId + mutate()` interleaving is gone.
- **A11y.** `<TextField label>` everywhere, `aria-label` on icon-only buttons, `aria-busy` on loading states, `role="group"` + `aria-label` on the matrix, MUI-default focus trap on the dialogs. The form inputs are labelled by MUI's input-label association.
- **Tests are behavior-focused.** `getByRole` / `getByLabelText` first; the only mock is the API client; the schema tests assert on the Zod error messages, not on the internal AST.
- **Server/Client boundary respected.** The alerts list page is a Server Component; the dialogs and matrix are client-side leaves. The per-alert detail page is also a client component, but the JSDoc explains *why* (the in-memory access token); the alternative (a Server Component fetch) would silently 401.
- **The wave 4 followup NIT-6 was investigated before being applied.** The conclusion (`globals: true` is actually needed because the `web/tests/*.test.ts` files use `describe`/`it`/`expect` as globals) is correct. That's the right kind of rigor.

### Summary

**Request changes.** Three criticals: (1) the new channel from inside the alert detail page doesn't invalidate the channels list, (2) the detail page has no `h1`, (3) the matrix's "missing row" vs "explicit Don't deliver" are conflated. The rest is solid — the structure is right, the test coverage is good, the tripwires are honored, and the deferred items are properly handed off. With the three criticals addressed, this is a clean wave 5 frontend ship.
